status: Frozen scientific design only; acquisition, collection and fitting require separate reviewed source releases.
purpose: Perform one finite representative calibration before natural-text validation. Failure of the old short-synthetic calibration on a new domain does not consume a method round. This finite budget does not establish convergence or impossibility of all variants.
data_separation: Only the 16 listed official TRAIN books may be acquired after a separate source approval. PG-19 validation16, PG-19 test32 and original synthetic TEST100 do not supply fitting or selection. No HellaSwag payload is authorized.
acquisition: Request each pinned GCS generation and verify the advertised size and base64 MD5. Preserve original bytes, SHA256, URL and UTC. Missing or changed objects are acquisition blockers; never substitute a book or generation silently.
text_preprocessing: Decode UTF-8 strictly. Normalize CRLF and then remaining CR to LF. Compute the Unicode-codepoint midpoint; begin after the first LF at or after it, or at the midpoint if none exists. Jointly tokenize the suffix with the pinned native model tokenizer, add_special=true, parse_special=false, no chat template. The first 768 IDs, including added special tokens, form the fixed ground-truth prefix. A shorter suffix makes calibration incomplete; do not replace the book or call this scientific failure.
old_seed_models: Bind old B canonical function and all eight old C/D model, preprocessing, source and library hashes before collection. Keep C/D fixed during collection. Each arm/book/subrun starts a fresh context and KV with the same immutable prefix IDs; hidden states, live routes and alpha evolve independently.

collection.prefix: Only B_pilotcanonical contributes all 768 prefix input states at each pilot layer. Old C/D compute their own 768-token prefixes to construct their KV, but their prefix states are not added.
collection.decode: B, old C and old D each generate at most 32 greedy tokens after their own prefix, with smallest-ID ties. Record EOG and stop without feeding it or manufacturing post-EOG states. Add all actual non-EOG-fed decode inputs from every arm. No error-, hit-, token- or prompt-based sampling.
collection.per_layer_nominal_formula: 16 * (768 + 3 * 32) = 13,824 is an upper bound. Natural EOG stopping may reduce it; never fill rows or replace books.
collection.state_identity: Typed provenance includes model, book, layer, arm, run/context, decode epoch, absolute input position, token ID and phase; retain actual current route IDs and final alpha. Old prompt groups and new book groups remain distinct.
collection.pool_semantics: Concatenate original FIT rows in their frozen order, then new rows in selected-book order: B prefix, B decode, old C decode, old D decode, each in absolute position order. Treat this as a multiset with unit weights, retaining identical rows and their provenance. Different arms from one book are not independent books.
collection.query_budget: Evaluate canonical f_e(X) for both selected experts at each model/layer on every new shared input row once per operator. All families share exactly those targets. Reuse old FIT targets only after input, weight and numerical identity checks. No additional family-specific state or target budget.
collection.decode_boundary: Logits at prefix position 767 select g0. For steps0..31: record the greedy token, stop before llama_decode if it is EOG, otherwise feed it at absolute position768+step and admit that actual input state. Thus every arm contributes0..32 decode input states; never pad after EOG.
collection.prefix_sampling_rationale: Use one canonical B prefix trajectory and three decode rollouts. C/D prefix states are not assumed identical at the second modified layer; their omission is a fixed sampling/weighting choice, not content-based deduplication.

fit.name: FIT120_plus_pg19train16_one_refresh; do not label it N120-only or 136 independent prompts.
fit.weights: Every old and new row has unit weight. All families use the same multiset. Statistical groups are original prompt ID or new book ID; generated arms are not separate books.
fit.preprocessing: Rebuild the shared depth-5 C32 tree, full-input leaf means and normal P128 once per layer on the complete combined FIT inputs, using the frozen algorithms, solver and seeds. Do not select between old and new geometry. Each refreshed operator registry binds the new preprocessing archive hash; the worker must not default to old Stage0 preprocessing.
fit.rowmask: Use an explicit mask covering every combined FIT row and typed row IDs. Do not call a legacy helper that filters prompt index < nfit=120 and would silently discard the new PG rows.
fit.fixed_role_registry: Keep the same eight operators, C32/r128/normal/unit weights/unguarded policy. Keep D roles PE6/G2 at q512 W8 host_floatlatent, selected before refresh by original VALID. No new rank, path, format, C or hyperparameter search; no PG validation selection.
fit.penalties: Carry the original per-operator pooled eta, local lambda and D global eta. Recompute covariance-trace-scaled ridge coefficients and all covariance/cross/eigen statistics on the new union; do not copy old numerical beta values.
fit.factor_fit: Use the frozen Mtarget top-512 eigenspace, sign/solver/cutoff/padding rules and fixed PE/G construction on the same union. Share targets and input statistics. This is not a required-minimum-rank or unrestricted-optimum claim.
fit.gauges: All eight selected D endpoints use identity. Freeze identity for all refreshed D fits. Do not select RMS versus identity on the new validation data.
fit.lowering: Preserve canonical W8/A8 and factor host FMA arithmetic. Recompute row quantizers and bias calibration using actual deployed predictions on the new FIT union; do not transfer old bias arrays.
fit.support: Record real runtime leaf occupancy, distinct groups, rank and conditioning. Never fabricate rows. Unsupported leaves use explicit canonical fallback and counts. An incomplete preprocessing or fit is inconclusive rather than automatic quality failure.
fit.outputs: Write fresh outputs in a unique Stage2 refresh directory. Preserve every seed, input and old model. Freeze new preprocessing/models, provenance, targets, fixed comparisons and dependency hashes before PG validation payload.
fit.sanity_before_validation: Before validation release, verify finite weights/scales/biases, complete operator/preprocessing identities and target hashes, real leaf occupancy split by old synthetic versus PG TRAIN, and reference/IPC B1-versus-batch controls. Preserve unsupported-region fallback counts. No validation data enters these checks.

later_quality: After valid tooling and this single representative refresh, compare C_refreshed to the unchanged B_pilotcanonical on the fixed 16 PG validation books; D_refreshed is secondary. Preserve the 2% relative custom-subset-PPL budget and two-model paired-book family. Always report transformation and total loss versus source. Old model diagnostics do not advance the round; a valid refreshed attempt can fail under the preset bounded rule without rejecting all guards or retraining variants.
optional_guard: Not part of the primary refreshed screen. No new guard search or failure based solely on coverage. A future guard would need an explicit TRAIN-only cutoff/map/policy freeze and complete fallback cost. PG validation never calibrates a guard.
resources: Only executor_sol implements, builds and runs candidate work after source approval. CPU only, eight physical cores for parent and children, sequential numerical work, no GPU. Offline collection/query/fit time, bytes and MACs are not deployed latency or 8GB runtime-residency evidence.
gates: Design only. Before book download or model contexts: source/build/synthetic review and explicit Root+critic COLLECT_REFRESH release. After collection closure: separate FIT_REFRESH release. Before validation: refreshed model/dependency freeze and a separate quality release. Repairs stay in Round2; no additional scientific failure or TEST access is implied.
